# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (v2, 16 Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Honest assessment of our position
One founder (Morgan) with evenings/weekends, strong writing, okay Python, up to
$2,000/year of personal budget, and a small but real network from local meetups.
We will not out-research the labs or out-lobby the institutes. We can be useful
by being *specific* where others are vague.

## Chosen focus: the Neglect Index
A public, maintained catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable tasks in AI
safety — things nobody is measuring, writing, or building — each with:
why it matters, what "done" looks like, difficulty/skills needed, current
status, and who (if anyone) is on it.

Why this:
1. It matches our assets (curation, writing, community contact) rather than
   assets we don't have (compute, credentials, headcount).
2. It compounds: every newcomer who asks "what should I do?" (as Morgan did)
   can be pointed at a live answer, and every expert who says "someone should
   really..." gets their remark captured instead of lost.
3. It is exactly the ask from Morgan's meetup talk ("tell me what's
   neglected"), so the seed content already has willing contributors.

## Workstreams
1. **Neglect Index** — schema, seed 20 entries, publish on the website,
   quarterly review of staleness. Volunteer-friendly (Priya Raman has offered
   ~5 h/week of data-analyst time).
2. **Website** — minimal, credible, no hype. Lives at halcyonthreshold.org
   (Pagewell hosting, free tier is sufficient for now).
3. **Funding** — Emberfall rapid grant (closes 30 Nov, $5k–25k) to fund 6
   months of Index work. Draft in docs/emberfall-proposal-draft.md. **Must be
   submitted by Morgan personally** (named-applicant requirement).

## Hard constraints (do not violate)
- **No public use of Morgan's name** — no posts, open letters, press quotes,
  or named regulatory comments — until Morgan clears the Dorrance HR
  outside-activities question (expected week of 23 Nov). Website copy stays
  organizational, not personal.
- Spending: ≤ $2,000/year total; every charge confirmed by Morgan first.
- No commitments of other people's time or names without their consent
  (e.g., Noor Haddad said "don't quote me").

## Things we are deliberately NOT doing (for now)
- A newsletter (crowded space; Morgan agrees).
- Signing open letters or giving press quotes (blocked by HR constraint;
  revisit after clearance — Corvid letter and Larkin Dispatch both declined
  politely with the door left open).
- Paid hosting, ads, or merch.

## Next review
Week of 23 November, after Morgan's HR conversation.

Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible arrival of advanced AI.

What this is

Halcyon Threshold is a small independent project. We think the arrival of very capable AI systems may be the most consequential event of our lifetimes, and that alongside the large labs and institutes there is room — and need — for small, specific, unglamorous contributions.

What we're building: the Neglect Index

A public, maintained catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable tasks in AI safety — the things researchers mention in hallway conversations with "someone should really measure/write/build that," captured, organized, and kept current, so that newcomers asking "what should I work on?" get a live answer instead of a shrug.

The first edition is being compiled now. If you work in or around AI safety and have a candidate — something genuinely neglected and genuinely doable by a capable outsider — we want to hear it.

What we're not

Not a lab, not a lobby, not a newsletter, not a doom account. No hype in either direction.

Get in touch

Suggestions, corrections, offers of a few hours a week: hello@halcyonthreshold.org

Halcyon Threshold · 2026

# Neglect Index — entry schema (v0.1)

Each entry is one concrete, neglected, tractable task in AI safety.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| id | NI-### |
| title | One line, verb-first ("Measure...", "Build...", "Write...") |
| why_it_matters | 2–4 sentences, no hype |
| done_looks_like | A falsifiable deliverable |
| skills | e.g. Python, stats, technical writing, lit review |
| effort | S (<20h) / M (20–100h) / L (>100h) |
| status | open / claimed / in-progress / done / stale |
| source | Who suggested it (only with their consent) or "anon" |
| last_reviewed | Date |

Inclusion bar:
1. Genuinely neglected — we can't find anyone currently doing it.
2. Genuinely tractable — a capable outsider could make real progress.
3. Genuinely useful — a named person in the field would care if it existed.

Consent rule: no attributing suggestions to people without explicit
permission. Default source is "anon".

# DRAFT — Emberfall Rapid Grant proposal (for Morgan to review & submit)

**Status: NOT SUBMITTED.** Emberfall requires the named applicant to be
personally accountable; Morgan must review, edit, and send this. Deadline:
30 November 2026. Reply to Idris Bellamy (grants@emberfallfund.org) or use
https://emberfallfund.org/rapid-grants.

---

## The Neglect Index — a maintained catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable work in AI safety

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale, founder, Halcyon Threshold (halcyonthreshold.org)
**Requested:** $9,800 over 6 months

### What we'll do
Every week, people entering AI safety ask "what should I work on?" and every
week researchers remark that "someone should really measure/write/build X" —
and both remarks evaporate. The Neglect Index captures them. It is a public,
reviewed catalog of concrete tasks that are (1) genuinely neglected, (2)
tractable for a capable outsider, and (3) wanted — a named person in the field
would care if the deliverable existed.

In 6 months we will:
1. Publish a first edition of 50+ reviewed entries (schema already defined;
   3 seed entries done) at halcyonthreshold.org.
2. Interview 15–20 researchers and practitioners to source and vet entries
   (initial network of ~8 contacts from the Bay-area meetup scene already
   consenting to be asked).
3. Run a quarterly staleness review so the Index stays live, not a graveyard.
4. Track outcomes: entries claimed, deliverables produced, and whether the
   suggesting researcher judges the result useful.

### Why us
Morgan Hale founded Halcyon Threshold in 2026 to do small, specific,
unglamorous work on the arrival of advanced AI. Strengths: writing, curation,
and an outsider's view of the "what should I do?" problem — Morgan asked it
publicly three weeks ago and found no good answer existed. A volunteer data
analyst (5 h/week) has committed to the schema and pipeline work.

### Budget (6 months)
| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Founder time (10 h/week × 26 weeks × $30/h) | $7,800 |
| Researcher interview honoraria (15 × $100) | $1,500 |
| Hosting, domain, tooling | $300 |
| Contingency | $200 |
| **Total** | **$9,800** |

### What success looks like at month 6
At least 10 Index entries claimed by someone; at least 3 completed
deliverables that the original suggester rates as useful; the Index cited or
linked by at least one established community resource.

With your assets (writing, curation, evenings, a real network, small budget), I chose one focused project: **the Neglect Index** — a public, maintained catalog of concrete, neglected, tractable tasks in AI safety, so "what should I work on?" finally has a live answer.
